subtitle: A hunter among floating islands

body: Solatorobo: Red the Hunter is CyberConnect2's Nintendo DS action role-playing adventure set among floating islands inhabited by doglike Caninu and catlike Felineko. Red Savarin works as a freelance hunter with his small machine, the Dahak, until an ordinary assignment draws him into a much larger mystery. The game shares its world with Tail Concerto and features character art by Nobuteru Yuki. Illustrated people, mechanical equipment and skybound settlements give the adventure a coherent personality, making a hired job feel like a doorway into a world with an everyday life of its own.

The Dahak's long arms can grab objects and enemies, then throw them into another target. Repeatedly catching and tossing an opponent builds a sequence of attacks, giving combat a distinctive physical rhythm. Purchased parts fit into upgrade slots, allowing the machine to be customised as more space becomes available. Red can also climb out to swim, use ladders or operate switches. The two scales complement one another: the machine provides strength, while its pilot can enter places and perform actions that the larger body cannot manage.

Side quests raise Red's hunter rank and open further progress, making local assignments part of the adventure's structure. A task may ask for an item, assistance to a resident or a different activity, providing reasons to visit the islands beyond the central mystery. Chikayo Fukuda's music and Madhouse's animated sequences support the story's changes in scale. Solatorobo gives its setting weight through that movement between jobs and discoveries. Red begins with practical work to complete, and the people encountered through it gradually make the wider conflict matter.
